runtime.projectApiCompatibilityEvidence: ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.asset has apiCompatibilityLevel: 6 and no per-platform override

scope.selectionBoundary: Gameplay, behavior, route planning, event-driven team autonomy, and parametric/modular authoring method only. No graphics replacement and no alternate engine.

evidenceClassificationLegend.directly_supported: Exact local file or primary upstream repository/documentation supports the claim.
evidenceClassificationLegend.contradicts_premise: Exact evidence shows the assumed gap or compatibility claim is false.
evidenceClassificationLegend.near_match_only: The tool addresses an adjacent need but does not prove fit for this exact project/runtime.
evidenceClassificationLegend.insufficient: A required compatibility or behavior claim has not been demonstrated.

localGapGraph.gap: Response-team routes are straight-line interpolation with no obstacle-aware path query.

evidence.fact: Three named anchors and three action targets feed Vector3.MoveTowards directly; the displayed task line has only two points.
The builder creates the three team destination anchors and starts all teams at a fixed concourse position.

localGapGraph.impact: This is the clearest mismatch with Frontier-style operational movement: commands are visible, but teams can cross geometry and cannot express corridor, door, stair, or congestion-aware routes.

localGapGraph.gap: Team jobs use a real queue, but lifecycle state is encoded as mutable strings and advanced by an Update-loop scan.

evidence.fact: Each team already has Queue<Job>, bounded enqueue/cancel/observe behavior, and a complete dispatch-arrival-interaction-release lifecycle.

localGapGraph.impact: The missing capability is typed, testable transitions and interruption semantics. A new job scheduler or behavior tree is not the first need.

localGapGraph.gap: World and interior authoring is parameterized in code but lacks a reusable parametric node graph or modular snapping authoring surface.

evidence.fact: The Blender world set is generated by fixed Python box/cylinder/mesh calls with explicit dimensions and loops.
Unity interior geometry is assembled by fixed transforms and persisted procedural meshes.

localGapGraph.impact: A parametric authoring add-on could speed controlled variants, but it would add a second authoring representation beside scripts and receipts.

candidates.name: DotRecast
candidates.category: runtime route planning and navmesh construction

facts: Core, Recast, and Detour 2026.3.1 target netstandard2.1 as well as newer standalone .NET targets.
Unity 6 documents support for managed plug-ins compiled for .NET Standard and exposes the .NET Standard 2.1 profile.
The library is managed C#, so macOS arm64 does not require a native architecture-specific binary.
runtimeCompatibility.unverifiedLimit: CHOOGuard has not compiled or run these assemblies yet; System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe dependency resolution and IL2CPP/player builds remain gates.

minimalInstall.preferred: Use pinned NuGet packages DotRecast.Recast 2026.3.1 and DotRecast.Detour 2026.3.1; allow the resolver to bring DotRecast.Core 2026.3.1 and the declared netstandard2.1 dependency only.
minimalInstall.restoreAction: After adding the pinned NuGetForUnity editor package below, run Unity menu NuGet > Restore Packages, then reopen/compile with the official installed Unity Editor.

specificWiringSeam.change: Add a bounded editor bake that converts only the reference-hall floor and explicit blockers into one Recast solo navmesh asset. Keep the three existing anchors as query endpoints.

On SetTaskTarget or team-location change, query a Detour path and store per-team corners; AdvanceAcceptedTime consumes accepted simulation delta along corners instead of moving directly to the final point. Render the existing task LineRenderer over all corners.
Keep allowUnsafeCode false initially. Add explicit precompiled references only if the resolver does not expose assemblies through auto-reference; do not widen all assemblies by default.

candidates.whyBetterThanExisting: It fills the exact missing route-query layer while preserving current anchors, queue semantics, accepted-time movement, animations, JuPedSim crowd physics, and command confirmation. It is substantially smaller than adopting another engine or a full crowd stack.
limits: Navmesh reachability is a gameplay route model, not validated emergency egress truth.
Do not replace JuPedSim crowd motion or FDS hazard computation with Detour crowd features in the first slice.
A larger open world would need tiled/streamed meshes later; that is outside the first migration.

candidates.name: UnityHFSM

facts: The upstream package is a Unity package with package.json version 2.3.0 and no native binaries.
The 2.3.0 release explicitly reports a fix for a Unity 6 import crash.
runtimeCompatibility.unverifiedLimit: CHOOGuard compilation and lifecycle equivalence tests have not been run.

minimalInstall.scope: One pinned UPM Git dependency; no samples imported initially.

specificWiringSeam.change: Replace Job.State string comparisons with a per-job StateMachine enum for Reserved, Validating, Dispatched, Moving, Interacting, AwaitingResult, Completed, Rejected, and Cancelled. Trigger transitions from IssueTeamCommand completion, route arrival, interaction completion, Observe result, hold, and cancel events.

candidates.whyBetterThanExisting: The current code already has FIFO queues and an explicit lifecycle, so a small HFSM maps directly to the actual gap. It adds typed transitions, guards, exit timing, and state-change events without introducing a blackboard/tree abstraction.
limits: Do not migrate the queue itself in the first step.
Do not add AI decision making until authoritative rules for autonomous choices exist.
The route planner remains the higher-impact gap.

candidates.name: Sverchok

facts: The pinned README explicitly lists Blender 4.5 support.
The add-on declares version 1.4.0 and is pure Blender Python.
runtimeCompatibility.unverifiedLimit: The pinned snapshot has not been enabled in local Blender 4.5.9 LTS, and optional nodes may need extra Python libraries.

minimalInstall.scope: Enable only from a project-local BLENDER_USER_SCRIPTS path; do not install optional dependencies for the first spike.

specificWiringSeam.change: Prototype one replaceable facade bay or stair module as a node group with explicit width, floor count, opening spacing, and metre outputs; export into the existing WorldSet folder and retain the current manifest/receipt checks.

candidates.whyBetterThanExisting: It offers live parametric variations and reusable node groups where the current builder requires Python edits. It is a method accelerator for repeated modules, not a replacement for the deterministic export and evidence scripts.
limits: The add-on is large relative to one prototype and overlaps existing Python generation.
GPL applies to the add-on and modifications; generated geometry licensing must still be reviewed separately.
Do not put core production generation behind unpinned master or optional numerical dependencies.

candidates.name: Building Tools

facts: The upstream release claims Blender 4.0 compatibility and provides a small release zip.
The project runs Blender 4.5.9 LTS, which upstream does not claim in the v1.0.13 README.
An upstream issue reports activation failure on Blender 4.0.2.
runtimeCompatibility.unverifiedLimit: Do not classify it compatible with Blender 4.5.9 until a project-local enable and one throwaway floorplan/floor/door/window operation pass.

minimalInstall.scope: Compatibility sandbox only; do not wire it into art/blender production scripts until the probe passes.

specificWiringSeam.change: If compatible, use its floorplan/floor/door/window operations only for a generic repeated building shell, then export through the existing metre and manifest checks.

candidates.whyBetterThanExisting: For ordinary shell modules it is smaller and more task-specific than a general parametric node system, with built-in floor, opening, roof, stair, and balcony operators.
limits: It does not provide Unity runtime snapping or emergency behavior.
The current authored station/interior scripts already cover fixed layouts, so value is limited to faster new shell variants.

companionDevtools.name: NuGetForUnity
companionDevtools.runtimeCompatibility: Its package declares Unity 2018.4 or newer; Unity 6000.3 exceeds that floor. It is an Editor package, not a shipped gameplay dependency.

projectLocalPinnedInstall.reason: Resolve and record the exact netstandard2.1 DotRecast DLL dependency graph inside the Unity project without installing a machine-global package manager.

limits: The standalone NuGetForUnity CLI is not immediately usable because dotnet is absent on this machine.
Fresh checkout can compile before restore; the upstream documentation calls this a known bootstrap limitation. Unity restore/compile must be part of the acceptance gate.

evaluatedButNotSelected.name: NPBehave 1.3.0
evaluatedButNotSelected.reason: It is legitimate MIT OSS and event-driven, but the local system already has queues and a linear job lifecycle. A behavior tree and blackboard would add a broader decision abstraction before there are authoritative autonomous branch rules; UnityHFSM is the closer fit.

evaluatedButNotSelected.name: DotRecast Detour.Crowd, Dynamic, TileCache, and Toolset
evaluatedButNotSelected.reason: Useful later for avoidance, dynamic obstacles, or world streaming, but the current three-team/reference-hall gap only needs a solo bake and path queries. JuPedSim already owns crowd modeling.

evaluatedButNotSelected.name: ufbx
evaluatedButNotSelected.reason: An independent FBX parser could inspect meshes, skinning, and animation data, but Blender and Unity already import the current civilian FBX files and local rig/metre receipts exist. Add it only if those importers disagree or a malformed-file gate becomes necessary.

recommendedNextBoundedMigration.name: One reference-hall route slice with DotRecast 2026.3.1
installSet: NuGetForUnity Editor package 4.5.0 pinned by Git tag
implementationBoundary: Bake one solo navmesh from the reference-hall floor plus explicit blockers.
Route one team from concourse to the existing warn target through at least one obstacle-forced turn.
Advance along path corners only from accepted simulation delta so pause/replay timing semantics remain intact.
Render the existing task line over the route corners.
Do not add Detour crowd, dynamic, tile cache, open-world streaming, autonomous decision policy, or a Blender add-on in this slice.
acceptanceEvidence: Unity 6000.3.23f1 imports/restores pinned assemblies and compiles ChooGuard.App with allowUnsafeCode=false.
A focused EditMode path query proves start/end projection, obstacle detour, and unreachable handling.
A focused PlayMode check proves the team never crosses the blocker, pause halts accepted-time travel, and arrival still triggers the existing interaction/release flow.
Record resolved package versions and hashes; label this gameplay route validation, not emergency-egress or field acceptance.
recommendedNextBoundedMigration.rollback: Remove the two DotRecast package entries and NuGetForUnity manifest entry, restore MvpStationView direct movement, and delete only the new owned navigation asset/files.

globalLimits: No candidate is claimed state of the art; this is a current, primary-source-verified fit shortlist.
No package, add-on, global config, credential, production source, or Unity asset was installed or changed in this lane.
Package compatibility is source-level until the pinned Unity Editor compile and focused runtime checks pass.
Route planning does not establish evacuation safety, official procedure compliance, real station geometry, or physical fidelity.
Blender add-ons must remain project-local and pinned; their outputs must pass existing metre, origin, rig, manifest, provenance, and Unity import checks.
Unity platform packages were not counted as OSI open source merely because their source is visible.
